explanation: The priestly garment that the high priest was to wear, consisting of several parts and adorned with precious stones.
A kind of apron or vest worn by the high priest, made from costly material and decorated with precious stones.
A square piece of cloth attached to the ephod, containing twelve precious stones representing the twelve tribes of Israel.
Mysterious objects kept in the breastpiece and used to seek God's guidance on important matters.
The highest religious leadership office among the people of Israel, responsible for performing sacrificial rituals and serving as a mediator between God and humanity.
An act in which animals, food, or other items are offered to God as a form of worship, thanksgiving, or atonement for sins.
The holy place where God dwelt among his people, first in the tabernacle and later in the temple in Jerusalem.
A ceremony in which persons, places, or objects are set apart and dedicated to God's service.
